findings.body: The lookup returns no record and the account passes the new blocklist check, allowing a trivial case-change bypass of the anti-abuse control.
findings.failure_mode: Semantically equivalent email addresses do not match the blocklist unless their bytes have identical casing.
findings.impact: The lookup returns no record and the account passes the new blocklist check, allowing a trivial case-change bypass of the anti-abuse control.
findings.root_cause: The blocklist performs a case-sensitive equality query against an unnormalized input.
findings.suggested_fix: Canonicalize both stored and queried addresses with the same normalization used for user emails, and enforce uniqueness on that canonical representation.
findings.title: Normalize addresses before querying the blocked-email table
findings.trigger: A blocked address is submitted with casing different from the corresponding `blocked_emails.email` row, such as `User@Example.com` versus `user@example.com`.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 12 shows `BlockedEmail.where(email: email).first` which performs case-sensitive comparison in most databases. The patch introduces this new code without normalization, allowing case-variant bypass of blocklist.

findings.body: The configured key is actually `user.blocked`, so users receive a missing-translation message instead of the intended validation error.

findings.impact: The configured key is actually `user.blocked`, so users receive a missing-translation message instead of the intended validation error.
findings.root_cause: The YAML entry is placed as a sibling of `email` rather than as its child.
findings.suggested_fix: Indent `blocked` to the same level as `not_allowed` so the resulting key is `user.email.blocked`, and assert the exact error text in the validator spec.
findings.title: Nest the blocked translation under the email key
findings.trigger: Validation rejects an address because `BlockedEmail.should_block?` returns true and requests `user.email.blocked`.
findings.verifier_reason: Line 734 shows `blocked: "is not allowed."` indented as sibling to `email:` (line 732), not nested under it. The validator at line 14 of email_validator.rb uses `:'user.email.blocked'` but YAML structure yields `user.blocked`, causing missing translation.

raw_findings.body: The statistics update joins the user's save transaction and is rolled back when the blocked-email validation makes that user save fail, leaving `match_count` and `last_match_at` unchanged for a real blocked attempt.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Whether a blocked match is recorded depends on whether validation was invoked inside or outside a save transaction.
raw_findings.impact: The statistics update joins the user's save transaction and is rolled back when the blocked-email validation makes that user save fail, leaving `match_count` and `last_match_at` unchanged for a real blocked attempt.
raw_findings.root_cause: A separate model is updated as a side effect of a validation that intentionally causes the enclosing persistence transaction to roll back.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Keep the validator side-effect free and record the blocked attempt outside the failed user-save transaction, such as at the account-creation/service boundary after validation reports the blocked error.
raw_findings.title: Do not persist blocklist statistics from inside validation
raw_findings.trigger: A blocked address is validated through `User#save` or `save!` without a preceding standalone `valid?` call, including service paths such as `User.create_for_email`.

raw_findings.body: Both processes can read the same count and save the same incremented value, so one match is lost and `match_count` under-reports blocked attempts.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Concurrent writes overwrite one another's counter updates.
raw_findings.impact: Both processes can read the same count and save the same incremented value, so one match is lost and `match_count` under-reports blocked attempts.
raw_findings.root_cause: The counter is incremented in application memory without locking or an atomic database operation.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Replace the read-modify-save sequence with one atomic SQL update, using an increment expression while setting `last_match_at`.
raw_findings.title: Increment match statistics atomically
raw_findings.trigger: Two account attempts validate the same blocked address concurrently.

raw_findings.body: The invalid row saves successfully and `should_block?` silently treats it as `do_nothing`, causing an address expected to be controlled by the table to fail open.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Invalid persisted enum values are accepted and interpreted as a non-blocking action.
raw_findings.impact: The invalid row saves successfully and `should_block?` silently treats it as `do_nothing`, causing an address expected to be controlled by the table to fail open.
raw_findings.root_cause: Only the email field is validated even though `action_type` is an enum with two supported values.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Add an inclusion validation for `action_type` against `BlockedEmail.actions.values`; add a database check constraint if records are expected to be loaded directly.
raw_findings.title: Reject unknown blocked-email action types
raw_findings.trigger: A record is imported or created with a non-null action value outside `BlockedEmail.actions`, such as `0` or `3`.

raw_findings.body: The other instance sees the same mutable array and incorrectly marks that address invalid despite never receiving the server rejection.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Validation state leaks between otherwise independent controller instances.
raw_findings.impact: The other instance sees the same mutable array and incorrectly marks that address invalid despite never receiving the server rejection.
raw_findings.root_cause: The mutable Ember array is constructed once in the class definition and shared by every instance.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Initialize `rejectedEmails` to a new `Em.A()` in the controller's `init` method after calling `_super`, rather than storing a mutable array on the prototype.

finding.trigger: More than one `CreateAccountController` instance is created in the same JavaScript runtime, such as across isolated application containers or controller tests, and one instance records a rejected address.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that multiple CreateAccountController instances share the same rejectedEmails array requires multiple controller instantiations in same runtime. Ember's extend() creates new instances with their own properties for primitive values, but arrays defined on prototype are shared. However, the trigger scenario of multiple isolated containers is speculative and the practical impact in normal Discourse usage is unsubstantiated.

However, the trigger scenario of multiple isolated containers is speculative and the practical impact in normal Discourse usage is unsubstantiated.
